subject: The Senate voted to hold Dr. Fauci in contempt
posts:
A Senate committee targets an 85-year-old retired official while ignoring broader executive overreach. 
Evidence: Oversight, Political theater, Distraction
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

The Senate committee claims this contempt vote is about enforcing accountability for pandemic-era policies. 
Stated Judgement: (0.5, 0.5) — Lesser Good

In reality, the move serves as a performative distraction from the committee's failure to address current executive branch abuses of power. 
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The committee uses a past figure to avoid confronting present constitutional crises. 
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.0, Uncertainty z: 2)
The Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt after he invoked his Fifth Amendment rights, refusing to testify on pandemic-era lab leak theories.

The Bright Side:
It highlights the rare, albeit misdirected, use of congressional oversight powers that have otherwise been dormant.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHO vs. WHAT error. They focus on a specific person (Fauci) to avoid the WHAT (the systemic executive overreach they are failing to regulate).

Social Physics Analysis:
By fixating on a retired official, the committee avoids the political cost of challenging the current administration. It is a classic projection of conflict onto a safe target to maintain the appearance of action.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The focus on past grievances prevents current systemic correction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Congress has the power to check the executive branch.

The Unavoidable Lie: Targeting a retired official is the most effective way to exercise that power.

Alethekanon:
This is a structural diversion. By focusing on a past figure, the committee abdicates its duty to address current, active executive overreach. It is a failure of logical prioritization.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see such energy spent on old battles while the country faces real, present-day struggles. We need healing and forward-looking leadership, not endless cycles of blame.

Brothekanon:
Classic move. When you don't want to fight the boss, you pick a fight with the guy who retired last year. It's all for the cameras, man.
